name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. 'tick' = per-frame animation tick; 'summon_anim_variant_a' = one of the 5 distinct summon-spell animation families (variant_a..e) in anisummn.c; '6slot' is a real structural dimension (the per-slot arrays frame_counter[6]/color_idx[6]/jitter[6]), not address residue. Consistent with siblings fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_b_6slot / _d_3slot / _e_16slot. No hex address suffix.
purpose: Per-tick state machine for the variant-A 6-slot summon-spell animation: 6 sprite slots with staggered start, mod-10 color rotation, and RNG-driven per-slot vertical jitter (0 or 7 px). Dispatch-table entry #4 of the 10-entry summon-spell tick table at 0x523B9.
logic_summary: Copies the 10-entry per-color Y-offset table (0x524A8) into a local; if the caster is on the enemy team (runtime_char[caster] offset+6 == 0) adds 0x8F to every local offset. Then dispatches on state_code: 0 (INIT) seeds the 6 slots' frame counters to -2*i (staggered) and color indices to i, sets each jitter byte to (rng()%2)*7, sets color_rotation_counter=6, clears terminate_flag, returns 2; 3 returns 0xC; 6 sets terminate_flag and returns 8; 2/5/8 (TICK) for each of 6 slots blits the current frame (when 0<=frame<7) at jitter+frame / origin_y+local_offset[color], fires a chime SFX at frame 0, increments frame, sets done_flag at frame 3, and at frame 8 (unless terminate_flag) advances color_rotation_counter mod 10 into the slot's color index, restarts the slot at frame 0, and re-rolls its RNG jitter; returns done_flag. Any other state_code returns 0.
signature: int fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot(uint32 caster_unit_id, uint32 sprite_handle, uint32 origin_y, uint32 row_stride, uint32 state_code)

params.name: caster_unit_id
params.semantics: Runtime-character index of the caster; used to index data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr to read the team byte (offset+6) for the enemy-team Y-offset shift.
params.reason: Accurately names the caster unit index; no address residue.

params.name: sprite_handle
params.semantics: Sprite atlas/handle passed as the first argument to fd2_blit_indexed_sprite for every per-slot blit.
params.reason: Matches its use as the blit sprite handle; no address residue.

params.name: origin_y
params.semantics: Base Y coordinate; the per-color local row offset is added to it to form the blit destination Y.
params.reason: Accurately names the base Y origin; no address residue.

params.name: row_stride
params.semantics: Destination row stride passed straight through as the stride argument to fd2_blit_indexed_sprite.
params.reason: Matches its use as the blit row stride; no address residue.

params.name: state_code
params.semantics: Animation phase selector dispatched on (0=INIT, 3, 6, 2/5/8=TICK frame, else no-op); read as a byte at [ESP+0x50].
params.reason: Accurately names the dispatched animation state; no address residue.

returns.semantics: Frame-hold / status code consumed by the caller's dispatch loop: 2 on INIT, 0xC on state 3, 8 on state 6, the per-tick done_flag (1 when any slot's frame hit 3, else 0) on TICK states, 0 otherwise.

notes: Source comment (anisummn.c lines 411-417) is already terse+accurate and matches the sibling variant_b/d/e comment style; kept as-is. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with the source understanding (RNG-driven jitter, dispatch table #4, all globals); left unchanged. Verified disassembly 0x26a55-0x26a71: jitter = (fd2_advance_rng_state() return % 2) * 7 (SAR/IDIV by 2, then SHL 3 / SUB = *7), confirming the source's 'EAX tracking bug corrected' note -- the Ghidra decompile's uVar2=var_14 conflation (loop index vs RNG return) is the known decompiler bug; the source is correct. Note on runtime_char team offset: code reads team at struct offset +6 (disasm MOVZX [EDX+EAX+0x6]); the fd2-knowledge strategy guide records the team field at +0x0E, but that guide is for a different FD2.EXE build (explicit version caveat) -- offset+6 is the consistent, ground-truth team read across all of anisummn.c for this FD2.LE binary, so the comment's 'bTeam (0=enemy)' label is correct. No logic changes made.
